PH-28
[ ] **Have the data handling policies reviewed by a qualified professional and publish the privacy notice and terms of use.**
**Status:** pending. **Owner:** project owner with qualified legal/privacy input.
**Dependency / trigger:** split from [PH-13](#ph-13) on 2026-10-22; PJ-13/PJ-14 before real customer or personal data, public signup or the Google consent screen ([PH-16](#ph-16)); PH-19 for the commercial terms.
**Request and reason:** Have a lawyer or privacy professional review the [data handling policies](data-handling-policies.md) against the actual operation. The review confirms or changes: the controller/processor roles, the retention durations (including the 5-year commercial ledger and the Marco Civil access-record question), the 15-day request deadline, incident notification to the ANPD and data subjects, and the international transfers to the listed providers. Then publish a privacy notice and terms of use in Portuguese, including the upload restrictions, at addresses the panel and consent screen can link. An agent can draft texts, but cannot give or replace legal advice.
**Configuration:** none. Do not put customer records or private advice in public documentation.
**Verification:** A dated record of the review's conclusions (not the private advice itself), the policies updated to match, and the published notice and terms reachable from the panel.
**Evidence / blocker:** 2026-10-22: policies decided under the owner's delegation; no review has taken place and no notice or terms are published.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Status and ownership
text:
Status and ownership
**Decided product policies, 2026-10-18:** the owner answered all 38 PH-11 questions directly. This document owns human enrollment, authentication assurance, recovery, sessions, permission allocation and support policy. The inherited [authentication](../security/authentication.md) and [authorization](../security/authorization.md) controls still govern. [Release policies](release-policies.md) own publication/playback behavior; this policy constrains who can trigger it.
**Accepted provider direction:** self-hosted Keycloak, with the [pinned-source compatibility assessment](identity-provider-evaluation.md#pinned-source-assessment) and owner acceptance recorded on 2026-10-18. Actual deployment remains subject to PH-10 host feasibility and PJ-24 integration qualification. No recurring identity/email procurement budget is authorized. This does not establish zero operating cost or an available email service. Google is the only selected external login provider; Microsoft is not part of this delivery.
**Accepted architecture:** the owner explicitly approved [ADR-0024](../adr/0024-propose-keycloak-and-server-managed-human-sessions.md) and [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-propose-application-owned-scoped-access-profiles.md) on 2026-10-18. They do not supersede accepted ADR-0012. **Implemented:** Keycloak login, server-managed sessions, OTP step-up and the first organization/access increment; [D-02 status](identity-session-design.md#implementation-status) and [D-01 status](tenant-data-design.md#implementation-status) own the implementation evidence and remaining workflows. PH-11 is completed for selection, and PH-20 records owner approval and the PJ-03/PJ-24 implementation request. External provisioning and unperformed release qualification remain pending.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Enrollment and account continuity
text:
Enrollment and account continuity
Support **public registration with automatic company activation** after verification and abuse checks, rather than requiring routine Teluni approval. The new company is separate from every existing company; matching a name, claimed business identifier or email domain never proves control of an existing tenant. Activation does not imply a free plan, trial duration, paid entitlement or unlimited resources. Completed PH-12 [commercial-policy selection](commercial-policies.md#pilot-and-public-trial) defines the bounded trial. Actual offer/capacity/coverage evidence remains PH-18, billing readiness PH-19 and notices PH-13 before public activation or applicable paid operation. A pending prerequisite must not silently turn the selected product into invitation-only onboarding.
Offer email/password and optional passkeys through the established identity provider, plus optional Google login. Do not make an external social account the sole administrative recovery method. Localized enrollment/login/recovery must support `pt-BR` and `en-US`.
Require trusted email verification before company access. Company invitations are recipient-bound, single-use, revocable and valid for **seven days**; a resend invalidates the previous pending invitation. Acceptance requires the matching authenticated identity and explicit membership confirmation. Changing recipient requires a new invitation. Verification establishes mailbox control, not legal identity or company ownership.
Link login methods only through an explicit flow proving the existing account and new method with recent authentication. Never merge accounts solely by equal email. A new email must be verified, the previous address notified and the stable application identity preserved. Method removal must leave a usable method meeting assurance requirements. This applies equally to first Google login and later linking.
One human identity may hold independent memberships in multiple companies and different scopes/roles within each. Switching company explicitly revalidates access. A company administrator cannot enumerate the person's other companies or manage their global credentials.
Each company has a **designated responsible administrator** who approves additional company administrators. Other administrators retain the matrix's ordinary administrative capabilities but cannot bypass that approval. Establish the first responsible administrator from the verified automatic signup flow; controlled assisted enrollment may serve support/migration needs without overriding the public-registration decision. Responsibility transfer requires an attributable, strongly authenticated flow and successor acceptance; prevent loss of the last active administrator or responsibility without a valid transfer. Responsibility is a company relationship, not an inferred legal-ownership determination or platform privilege.
Provision platform administrators through a controlled procedure, outside public signup and tenant administration. Use individual administrative accounts distinct from ordinary customer operation, with phishing-resistant assurance and prepared recovery. Product administration does not grant access to provider administration, infrastructure, database credentials or customer content.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Assurance, recovery and abuse
text:
Assurance, recovery and abuse
Strong authentication is mandatory for platform administrators, company administrators and branch managers. Operators may opt in, and companies can require it for everyone. Any operator/profile granted publication or automatic-price distribution must also meet the strong-authentication requirement. Do not let custom role labels bypass an assurance requirement attached to a capability.
Prefer passkeys with user verification; password plus an authenticator-app second factor is the selected alternative, with protected single-use recovery codes. Platform administration requires a phishing-resistant method and protected recovery. Social login or a generic passkey label does not alone prove equivalent assurance: qualify the actual flow and assertion. Email-only recovery cannot bypass mandatory MFA. Do not use SMS as the default method.
Require strong authentication no more than **five minutes** old when promoting administrators, changing credentials/MFA/email, transferring responsibility, granting support access, exporting in bulk or unlinking/destroying in bulk. Ordinary authorized publication/price operations use the normal compliant session, without a new prompt for every save. Sensitive operations by users without an enrolled adequate factor must first obtain the required assurance. Confirmation dialogs do not constitute authentication.
Use provider-owned password recovery with enumeration-safe public responses. The selected reset-link target is **15 minutes**, single-purpose and single-use; verify exact invalidation semantics in the selected version. Successful password recovery revokes earlier sessions. MFA recovery first uses a valid alternate authenticator or recovery code. Suspected compromise offers global session termination and a support channel.
Complete loss of recovery methods uses exceptional assisted recovery with proportionate evidence, waiting/notification to previous channels, review and audit. The operational procedure, waiting interval, evidence criteria and escalation remain to be reviewed before use; no instant-unlock promise is made. Seek independent review for higher-risk cases when available, without claiming a two-person control in a one-person operation. Insufficient evidence denies access. Do not introduce personal security questions, agent-created temporary passwords or email-only removal of MFA. Company administrators may repair local membership but cannot reset another person's global identity. Prepare a separate accountable recovery path for the sole platform administrator/last responsible company administrator.
Apply context/operation rate limits, progressive delays, enumeration-safe responses and monitoring, without permanent attacker-triggered lockout. Additional challenges need demonstrated need, accessibility/privacy review and cost approval; they are not a default on every interaction. Numerical anti-abuse limits and provider password-policy parameters require technical review rather than invented vendor defaults. No external challenge subscription is authorized.

List sessions using minimized, justified metadata; allow termination of one or all. Background polling/refresh does not count as human activity and cannot extend absolute duration. Warn before timeout and protect recoverable drafts without leaking them across account/company changes or retaining protected caches after logout. Detailed concurrent-session accounting across provider and application sessions remains design/qualification work.
**Accepted browser architecture, implemented by the identity module:** server-managed application sessions with an opaque protected browser cookie; provider access/refresh tokens remain server-side. Compose this capability into the modular backend where appropriate rather than adding a microservice by default. Use established OIDC Authorization Code with PKCE and established session/security components; do not invent token issuance, crypto or password handling. Evaluate `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`, narrow cookie scope, explicit CSRF protection, state/nonce/redirect validation, fixation prevention, refresh rotation/replay/concurrency, logout propagation and token minimization. [D-02](identity-session-design.md#implementation-status) records the concrete controls and remaining qualification; the API contracts and configuration schema own route/cookie/configuration facts.
The internal API bearer boundary remains ADR-0012. A browser cookie must terminate at a reviewed session boundary that obtains the legitimate issuer access token; it is not a second implicit credential accepted by every domain route. The current verifier returns principal ID/scopes, not session or assurance evidence; extend integration contracts deliberately through technical review rather than trusting browser-supplied session IDs, role flags, timestamps or MFA claims.
Validate current application account/session/membership state in addition to JWT signature/expiry to meet the 30-second bound. Cache invalidation, session linkage and sensitive-write race handling need explicit implementation evidence. A valid five-minute JWT alone cannot satisfy that bound. Provider logout and application logout must be reconciled, including reuse/replay and local/global termination. Human logout does not revoke unrelated company memberships or player identities.
On provider, email or session infrastructure failure, unavailable flows report a safe temporary failure. Existing operations continue only while trusted identity, validity and authorization can still be established; otherwise deny protected operations and preserve recoverable work safely. A key/session-store outage is not permission to skip checks. There is no offline administrative panel or public emergency credential. Players retain their independently selected bounded offline policy, not these human-session limits.

Support readable default roles plus company-customized profiles built from explicit business capabilities and scopes. The application owns memberships, profiles and resource authorization, not arbitrary provider groups or self-editable identity attributes. Check company, branch, resource, operation, assurance and current state on the server, including background jobs and generated data. This is a product policy; the accepted technical direction is ADR-0025; its concrete mechanism and verification remain implementation work.

Newly created branches do not silently enter a restricted branch grant. Company-wide administrative scope is an explicit grant. Avoid arbitrary negative-rule languages, cyclic inheritance or an unrestricted role shortcut. Grantors cannot confer authority they lack; company grants never confer platform authority. Profile edits must show affected users/scopes and be audited.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Publication impact and delayed work
text:
Publication impact and delayed work
An authorized designated price save triggers automatic publication under PH-09. Before accepting it, authorize the mutation **and all affected published targets**. If any target is outside scope, **reject the entire price mutation** with a safe explanation. Do not partially distribute it, modify the company base price anyway or create an out-of-scope approval request as an automatic fallback. An explicit authorized branch override may be used only when the model and local impact permit it. A permitted shared edit cannot grant hidden publication power.
Authorized publishers normally publish directly. A company may optionally require independent approval by branch/operation; default is disabled, with no self-approval where required. For covered prices, entering a proposal is not saving an effective price: the authorized approval commits that price and triggers automatic publication. This explicit policy qualifies the PH-09 save behavior without turning ordinary drafts into live content. P27 still requires denying an out-of-scope price mutation; optional approvals do not provide a bypass. Approval-chain configuration must identify eligible reviewers, prevent scope escalation and clearly distinguish proposed, approved, saved, queued and active states. No approval module is implemented or inherited from Orion's removed reference feature.
Revalidate company/actor/target authority before an outstanding intent effects a protected change/publication. If authority has been removed/reduced, block the not-yet-effected intent and require new attributable authorization, retaining original authorship. A valid version already authorized and issued continues its normal delivery lifecycle; removing its author does not automatically cancel company programming. Incident response may revoke specific publications/identities. Revalidation cannot silently expand old targets or allow stale work to overwrite newer generations.
Company administrators remove only the local membership; other memberships and global identity remain. Departure does not delete company content. Global disablement is an identity operation. Company suspension denies new protected server operations, with explicit reconciliation for already-authorized offline players; [Commercial policies](commercial-policies.md#payment-expiry-cancellation-and-retention) own commercial/cancellation consequences and distinguish limited commercial access from security suspension; PH-18/PH-19 retain real offer/billing readiness. Historical attribution remains meaningful subject to PH-13 retention/deletion rules. Never promise instantaneous erasure of unreachable devices.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Support, audit and continuity
text:
Support, audit and continuity
The [commercial support policy](commercial-policies.md#hardware-onboarding-and-support) owns coverage/service boundaries; actual coverage remains unverified under PH-18. Routine customer-content support requires an explicit company-administrator grant: reason, scope, maximum default duration **one hour**, read-only default and separate write authority. Support uses its own identity, with visible/audited activity; **no impersonation in this delivery**. Platform operations may manage customer lifecycle metadata without implicit content browsing. A support grant never authorizes provider/database/infrastructure access.
Emergency access requires a distinct exceptional procedure with justification, strong authentication, scope, expiry, audit and notification afterward where applicable. It creates no permanent secret user, universal password or unrestricted standing customer-content access. Evidence criteria, available reviewers and execution/revocation steps must be reviewed before use, honestly reflecting team size. A routine support grant is not emergency authority.
Users can review their sessions and receive relevant credential/recovery notices. Company administrators see company-scoped audit; branch managers see only their branch operations. The platform receives minimized events needed for security/operation. Audit invites, grants/profile changes, assurance/recovery/revocation, support, prices/publications and relevant failures with actor/scope/action/outcome, excluding secrets and full payloads. Security-audit retention and metadata such as IP remain PH-13; the PH-09 operational-report retention is not a legal/security retention decision.
Require application-stable principal IDs, application-owned memberships/permissions, isolated environments and synthetic test identities. Back up/restore identity state under PH-10 and reconcile revocations after restoration. Portability is required, but P37=A does **not** require a pre-pilot export/import proof as a separate acceptance gate; qualify migration when selected/needed and document available mechanisms/limits. A migration may require safe password reset or authenticator reenrollment; do not promise export of every factor or session. No production credentials in CI or cross-environment token acceptance.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Required verification cases
text:
Required verification cases
These are specified allow/deny and lifecycle cases, **not executed tests**. PJ-03/PJ-24 own implementation evidence; PJ-07 owns design review.
Case
Required expected result
IA-01 — Public enrollment
Verified eligible signup creates a new isolated company and its responsible administrator; cannot claim an existing tenant, set privileged principal claims or gain platform authority
IA-02 — Invitation and linking
Correct verified recipient accepts once within seven days; wrong recipient, replay, revoked/replaced/expired invite and email-only account merging fail
IA-03 — Company context
One identity uses independently scoped memberships; switching/reusing IDs, mixed-tenant references, collections, counts, downloads and caches cannot cross scope
IA-04 — Responsibility
Responsible administrator approves additional administrators; ordinary admin cannot bypass it; last-admin removal and incomplete transfer fail
IA-05 — Assurance
Required roles/capabilities cannot bypass MFA; sensitive actions require trusted assurance no older than five minutes; social/weak recovery cannot satisfy it implicitly
IA-06 — Recovery
Reset-link expiry/single use, MFA recovery and earlier-session revocation work; insufficient assisted-recovery evidence cannot grant access or affect unrelated memberships
IA-07 — Sessions
Idle/absolute limits, no remember-me, five-session/two-platform-context bounds and explicit termination work across tabs, refresh concurrency and logout
IA-08 — Revocation
Global/session/local removal and profile reductions prevent new operations within 30 seconds; stale JWT/grants cannot authorize sensitive effects; unrelated memberships remain available
IA-09 — Browser boundary
OIDC state/nonce/PKCE/redirect checks, protected cookies, CSRF/fixation controls, token redaction and server-only token storage resist bypass; provider logout/refresh replay are reconciled
IA-10 — Scoped profiles
Matrix allow cases work; operator publish/delete/export, manager cross-branch actions, unauthorized grants/profile edits and temporary-grant expiry fail closed
IA-11 — Price impact
Authorized all-target save publishes; any unauthorized target rejects the whole mutation without a partial save/distribution or hidden approval fallback; authorized local override stays local
IA-12 — Optional approvals
Disabled policy allows authorized direct publication; enabled policy requires independent scoped approval and never labels a price proposal already effective
IA-13 — Delayed work
Removal/reduction blocks an outstanding protected effect; issued valid publications continue normally; retries do not expand scope or lose real authorship
IA-14 — Support/emergency
No default customer-content privilege; scoped consent expires within its grant, read grants cannot write, no impersonation, exceptional access follows separately reviewed controls
IA-15 — Failure and continuity
Identity/JWKS/session/email outages fail safely without administrative bypass; environments, restore and migration preserve principal scope/revocation and independent player behavior
IA-16 — Evidence and abuse
Safe public errors, bounded abuse controls, audit access/notifications and redaction preserve attribution without enumerating identities or leaking secrets

heading: Evaluation scope and result
text:
Evaluation scope and result
On **2026-10-18**, the owner selected self-hosting and **Keycloak**, then explicitly approved all pending Teluni ADRs, including ADR-0024/ADR-0025. Host feasibility and actual integration qualification remain delivery prerequisites. No recurring identity/email procurement budget is available. This is a documentation/source review, not a deployed-provider experiment, security assessment or proof of operational capacity. Keycloak **26.8.1**, release published on 2026-10-13, was inspected at source commit `24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b` for the assessment below. This pins review evidence only; no deployment image/digest has been selected or installed. Reassess the deployment version and security status before implementation; mutable `latest` documentation does not pin a production dependency.
The existing [verifier](../../apps/api/src/authentication.ts) and accepted [ADR-0012](../adr/0012-verify-jwt-access-tokens-at-the-first-api-boundary.md) are the executable/governing boundary. Do not weaken it because a candidate emits different defaults. The source/documentation review and explicit owner approval satisfy PH-11's architectural decision scope. They do not qualify a running integration. Required policies and measured bounds remain in the [identity policy](identity-and-access.md), not vendor defaults.

Mapping a UUID-looking user-editable attribute is insufficient. Pin principal creation, authoritative ownership, `(issuer, subject)` association, uniqueness and migration semantics during design. Do not add machine-client grants to a human client and assume a hardcoded actor mapper distinguishes them. Provider roles may inform trusted mapping but cannot replace current application memberships/resource permissions.

title: Teluni Identity Provider Evaluation
heading: Pinned-source assessment
text:
Pinned-source assessment
Evidence was read from the official [26.8.1 release](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/releases/tag/26.8.1) and the immutable source commit above. Nine Java source files were downloaded outside the repository for inspection; no downloaded code was executed, provider started or token issued. This is a supported architectural compatibility assessment, not an interoperability test.
Existing API requirement
Pinned-source evidence / accepted integration responsibility
Exact `typ=at+jwt`
[DefaultTokenManager](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/jose/jws/DefaultTokenManager.java) selects the RFC 9068 access-token header when the client option is enabled; [OIDCConfigAttributes](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/OIDCConfigAttributes.java) defines `access.token.header.type.rfc9068`. Configure it explicitly; do not change the existing verifier's accepted type
Signed tokens and exact issuer/audience
The signing path in DefaultTokenManager uses the configured signature provider. [TokenManager](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java) sets issuer; [SubMapper](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/SubMapper.java) supplies the persistent user subject; [AudienceProtocolMapper](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AudienceProtocolMapper.java) adds the configured audience. The integration must select RS256 or ES256 and the exact trusted API issuer/audience/JWKS, then test actual signatures/key rotation and denial cases
`sub`, `iat`, `exp`, string `scope`
TokenManager initializes access tokens from the authenticated user/session and sets the scope string; [AccessToken](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/representations/AccessToken.java) and [JsonWebToken](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/representations/JsonWebToken.java) define their representation/time lifecycle. Actual emitted types, clock bounds and expiry remain verifier integration tests
Application principal UUID
[UserAttributeMapper](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/UserAttributeMapper.java) maps a configured user attribute into a configured token claim. Trusted provisioning must generate an application UUID, keep a unique stable `(issuer, subject)` association and map a non-user-editable attribute to `orion_principal_id`. User profile edits, signup, Google imports and tenant administrators cannot create/replace that attribute; fail closed until the trusted mapping exists
Trusted human assertion
[HardcodedClaim](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/HardcodedClaim.java) can supply `orion_actor_type=human` only in a restricted human-login client/flow. Disable service-account, password/direct-grant and unreviewed exchange/impersonation paths on that client; a constant mapper alone does not prove a human. Test that machine credentials cannot produce an accepted human token
Session/assurance freshness
The current verifier deliberately returns only principal/scopes. The reviewed OIDC boundary must bind verified login assertions and current server session/assurance state to that principal and the legitimate access token. An ID token may establish login context at its intended OIDC boundary but never substitutes for the API access token. Enforce the 30-second session/membership revocation goal using application state, not unimplemented claims or provider logout alone
The review found a viable standards-based mapping path without changing ADR-0012. It does not assert that a default Keycloak client/token already meets the contract. Immutable principal provisioning, protected profile attributes, human-only flow restrictions and trusted session/assurance binding are mandatory implementation design/control requirements under PJ-07/PJ-24, not controls that were deployed in this task. Deployment version/image selection remains PH-15/PJ-24.

title: Teluni Identity Provider Evaluation
heading: Alternatives and tradeoffs
text:
Alternatives and tradeoffs
Direction
Assessment for the current decision

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Approved detailed design for D-02, 2026-10-18.** The owner approved it as proposed under [PH-20](human-actions.md#ph-20). It turns accepted ADR-0024 (Keycloak, server-managed browser sessions) and ADR-0025 (application-owned access) into concrete trust boundaries, flows, state and controls, and preserves accepted ADR-0012 unchanged. It answers the [new authentication mechanism checklist](../security/authentication.md#new-authentication-mechanism-checklist). PJ-24 implements it incrementally; [implementation status](#implementation-status) separates what exists and is qualified from what remains. A Keycloak behavior below is established only where that section names the passing test.
Out of scope here: company, membership, grant and invitation semantics ([tenant data design](tenant-data-design.md) and the organizations implementation conventions), invitation email delivery (specified by the approved D-13 [invitation and email delivery design](invitation-delivery-design.md) under the [delivery policy](../architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md)), player/device credentials (D-03) and real environment provisioning (PH-15–PH-17).

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Components and trust boundaries
text:
Components and trust boundaries
Component
Responsibility
Holds

Credentials, registration, email verification, MFA/passkeys, recovery, Google brokering (after PH-16), token issuance

No new service, broker or cache is introduced. Keycloak runs as a separate process on the same host (ADR-0021), with its own database under PH-10/PH-15.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Keycloak configuration contract
text:
Keycloak configuration contract
The realm definition is committed without secrets and applied by an idempotent provisioning script; test fixtures generate synthetic client secrets per run. Production values come from PH-15. The realm uses the `teluni` login theme, a child of Keycloak's `keycloak.v2` theme that changes styles (palette, typeface and mark from the [branding guide](branding/README.md)) and one page, the new-password page, which always ends the person's other sessions (P15); its files live in [`apps/api/keycloak/themes/teluni`](../../apps/api/keycloak/themes/teluni/login/theme.properties), and every Keycloak that serves the realm, including a real deployment under PH-15, installs them.
**Realm.** Public registration enabled (P06); email as login identifier; duplicate emails disallowed; email verification required before any code is issued (P07). Brute-force detection uses temporary lockout with increasing waits and never permanent lockout (P36). Password policy is minimum length 12, maximum 128, not equal to username or email, with no composition rules (approved under PH-20). Required actions: verify email, configure OTP, passkey registration and recovery codes. The reset-credentials action token lasts 15 minutes and is single-use (P15). Refresh-token rotation is on with zero reuse. SSO session limits never exceed the application's (12-hour maximum).
**Declarative user profile.** Unmanaged attributes are disabled. The `orion_principal_id` attribute is viewable and editable by administrators only, absent from registration and account forms, and validated as a UUID, so users, signup, brokered imports and company administrators cannot create or replace it.
**Assurance levels.** The browser flow maps `teluni-aal1` (password, or Google once enabled) and `teluni-aal2` (password plus OTP or recovery code, or a passkey with user verification) through Keycloak's level-of-authentication conditions. A step-up request for `teluni-aal2` makes a user without an adequate factor enroll one before completing (P12/P13).
**`teluni-web` client.** Confidential; standard flow with mandatory PKCE `S256`; direct access grants, implicit flow, service accounts, device and CIBA grants, token exchange and impersonation disabled; one exact redirect URI per environment at the API callback; no web origins (all provider calls are server-side); front-channel logout off and back-channel logout on with session required; RFC 9068 `at+jwt` access-token header enabled; access-token lifetime five minutes (P20); full scope disabled. A dedicated client scope adds the API audience, maps `orion_principal_id` from the protected attribute, adds the constant `orion_actor_type=human` only on this human-login client, and emits `acr`, `auth_time` and `amr` in the ID token.
**`teluni-provisioner` client.** Confidential; service account only, every login flow disabled. Its service account holds `view-users` and `manage-users` in the realm-management client and nothing else. These roles grant user management as a whole, broader than setting one attribute; PJ-24 checks whether the pinned version's fine-grained administrative permissions can narrow them. Its credential is `RESTRICTED`, used only by principal provisioning, audited through Keycloak admin events and never present in the browser or in tests beyond synthetic values. A Keycloak extension that generates the identifier internally was considered and rejected for now: it adds a Java build, deployment and upgrade coupling.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Principal provisioning
text:
Principal provisioning
The application, not Keycloak, creates the stable principal UUID required by ADR-0012, and PostgreSQL is its authority.
The callback exchanges the code (state, nonce and PKCE validated by the client library) and verifies the ID token. An unverified email is denied.
The identity module inserts `principals (id, issuer, subject)` with a new random UUID under `UNIQUE (issuer, subject)`, using `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` followed by a read, so concurrent first logins converge on one principal.
If the provider access token lacks `orion_principal_id`, the module reads the Keycloak user. It sets the attribute to the database principal ID only when the attribute is absent; a different existing value fails closed and records a security event. It then refreshes the tokens.
The refreshed access token must pass the unchanged ADR-0012 verifier with exactly the database principal ID. Until it does, no session becomes active.
Google brokering (after PH-16) uses a first-broker-login flow that links an existing account only after re-authentication of that account; email-based automatic linking is removed and the Google identity provider does not mark emails as trusted (P08). Global disablement is a platform operation that sets the principal disabled in PostgreSQL, which denies immediately, and disables the Keycloak user, reconciled if that call fails.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Server-managed sessions
text:
Server-managed sessions
Property
Design
Credential
32 random bytes, base64url, in the session cookie. The database stores only its SHA-256 hash and never the recoverable value
Stored state
Principal, provider session ID (`sid`), state, creation, last human activity, absolute expiry, assurance level, last strong-authentication time, encrypted provider tokens, provider check time and a refresh lease
Provider tokens
Refresh, access and ID-token-hint values encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a key ring from `RESTRICTED` configuration; a key identifier per value allows rotation with overlap
Idle limit
30 minutes when the principal holds an administrative or branch-manager grant in any active membership, or has no membership; two hours when every active membership is operator access, including operators with additional grants (P17). Applying the stricter limit across memberships avoids trusting a client-selected company for session lifetime; switching company is revalidated per request by the [tenant data design](tenant-data-design.md#request-scope-resolution). Background polling marks requests as non-activity and never extends the session
Absolute limit
12 hours, or a shorter company setting when one exists (P17); no remember-me and no persistent cookie lifetime (P18)
Session count
At activation, a principal with five active sessions gets a pending session that can only list and terminate sessions until one is ended; activation locks the principal row to serialize concurrent logins (P19). The two-context platform limit applies when platform accounts exist
Termination
The user ends one or all sessions; password recovery and provider-side logout arrive by back-channel logout; global disablement and refresh failure revoke; membership removal denies company access without ending the session
Logout
Revoke the application session, end the provider session server-side with the refresh token, clear the cookie. A provider failure still leaves the application session revoked and is reported diagnostically

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Session boundary for API requests
text:
Session boundary for API requests
Product modules that need a human require a session; a bearer-only request without a session is rejected with `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`, because the 30-second session-termination bound cannot be enforced for it. For each request the boundary runs, in order:
Request limiting (already required before authentication), then cookie parsing and lookup by hash: active, not expired by idle or absolute limit, principal active.
For unsafe methods, CSRF validation (below).
Provider revalidation: if the provider was last checked more than 30 seconds ago, introspect the stored access token with the client credentials; inactive means revoke and deny. If the access token has under 60 seconds left, refresh under a single-flight database lease; concurrent requests wait briefly for the winner and otherwise fail as temporarily unavailable rather than skip the check. `invalid_grant` revokes the session; network or provider failure fails closed with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` without revoking.
Run the stored access token through the unchanged ADR-0012 verifier and require its principal ID to equal the session's principal.
Record human activity when applicable and pass a minimal context to the module: principal ID, session ID, assurance level and last strong-authentication time. Domain code never sees cookies or provider tokens.
Together with per-request membership resolution in the [tenant data design](tenant-data-design.md#request-scope-resolution), this bounds global disablement, session termination and membership reduction to 30 seconds (P20, IA-08). The cost is availability coupling: if Keycloak is unreachable, protected panel operations stop within 30 seconds by design (P22). Players are unaffected.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Assurance and step-up
text:
Assurance and step-up
Assurance comes only from the ID token verified at the callback (signature, issuer, client audience, nonce): `acr` sets the session level and, for `teluni-aal2`, `auth_time` becomes the last strong-authentication time. Browser-supplied flags are never trusted.
The organizations capability declares which grants require strong authentication (administrators, branch managers and any publication or automatic-price capability, P12) and which operations require strong authentication no older than five minutes (P14). The API answers missing assurance with new public codes (`STRONG_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` or `RECENT_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`, 403) and no state change. The panel then starts a step-up login requesting `teluni-aal2` and, for recency, `max_age=0`. The callback checks that the requested level and recency were met, rotates the session credential (fixation defense on elevation) and updates assurance. A company option can require strong authentication for all members.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Browser protections
text:
Browser protections
**Cookies.** Session: `__Host-` prefixed, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`, no `Max-Age`. Login attempt: `__Host-` prefixed, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` (it must accompany the provider redirect), 10-minute lifetime. Development and test over loopback HTTP may drop the prefix and `Secure`; production configuration rejects a non-HTTPS public origin.
**CSRF.** Unsafe methods require an `Origin` header equal to the configured public origin and an `X-CSRF-Token` header equal to an HMAC of the session ID under a configured key, compared in constant time. The panel obtains the token from the no-store session endpoint and keeps it in memory.
**Login integrity.** State, nonce and PKCE verifier live server-side in a single-use attempt row bound to the login-attempt cookie; the callback consumes it with a conditional update and rejects reuse or expiry. A new session credential is always minted at the callback, replacing any existing one.
**Redirects and leakage.** The return path accepts only same-origin relative paths; otherwise `/`. Authentication responses use `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; the callback redirects immediately so the code does not linger. Cookies, codes and tokens are never logged, consistent with the existing raw-URL and header redaction.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Back-channel logout
text:
Back-channel logout
Keycloak posts a logout token to the API when a provider session ends (logout elsewhere, administrator action, password recovery that ends other sessions). The endpoint verifies signature, issuer, client audience, freshness, the back-channel logout event and absence of a nonce; rejects a replayed `jti`; and revokes sessions by provider `sid`, or every session of the subject when no `sid` is present. It is rate-limited and exempt from CSRF because it is a server-to-server call.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Routes and module composition
text:
Routes and module composition
The identity module serves, under the API's existing `/api` path prefix: login start (including step-up), callback, session summary with CSRF token, logout, list and terminate own sessions, and back-channel logout. Exact paths, schemas and new error codes are defined as executable contracts in PJ-24 and published through OpenAPI.
This is the first collaboration between API modules. `modules.ts` constructs the identity module first and passes its session-boundary port into dependent module factories. The shared [module contract](../../apps/api/src/module.ts) gains one narrow addition: a module can declare that it requires another module, and activation skips it outside production, or refuses to start in production, when that module did not activate. No dependency-injection framework or global registry is introduced.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Libraries and configuration
text:
Libraries and configuration
**OIDC client:** `openid-client` (OpenID-certified relying-party library by the author of the `jose` library the verifier already uses), current major pinned at implementation. It performs discovery, PKCE, state/nonce validation, code exchange, refresh, introspection and ID-token validation.
**Cookies:** `@fastify/cookie`, used only for parsing and serialization.
**Not used:** generic Fastify session plugins. Stateless encrypted cookies cannot be revoked, and server-store plugins still need a custom store while lacking the selected session-count, per-role idle, assurance and revocation semantics. Session state remains ordinary application data; all cryptography uses Node's standard primitives (random bytes, SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256, AES-256-GCM), with no custom algorithm.
**Configuration:** a public HTTPS origin; OIDC client credentials, provisioner credentials and the session/CSRF key ring, all `RESTRICTED`; existing issuer, audience and JWKS settings reused. Names and schemas are added to the canonical [API configuration](../generated/configuration/api.md) only when implemented.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Local development and automated qualification
text:
Local development and automated qualification
Integration and browser tests start disposable containers, as PostgreSQL already does: Keycloak 26.8.1 (`quay.io/keycloak/keycloak`, pinned by digest at implementation, after rechecking its security status) with a generated test realm, and Mailpit as a local SMTP sink for verification and recovery mail. A manual local stack starts the same containers with the API and Vite and prints URLs, using synthetic users only. No production credential is needed in development or CI.
Case
Verification in PJ-24
IA-01, IA-02 (identity part)
Browser signup through the Keycloak pages with Mailpit verification; principal provisioning races; email-only linking rejected
IA-05
Step-up to `teluni-aal2` with OTP enrollment; recency at five minutes; aal1 denied for strong-authentication capabilities
IA-06
Reset link expires after 15 minutes and is single-use; recovery ends earlier sessions through back-channel logout
IA-07
Idle, absolute and pending-session-limit behavior across tabs and concurrent refresh; no remember-me
IA-08
Session termination, global disablement and Keycloak-side logout deny within 30 seconds; stale tokens rejected
IA-09
State/nonce/PKCE/redirect tampering, login-attempt replay, cookie attributes, CSRF/Origin rejection, fixation, token redaction
IA-15
Keycloak, JWKS and database outages fail closed with safe errors and recover
Each Keycloak assumption in this document (header type, protected attribute mapping, human-only client restrictions, level-of-authentication step-up and OTP enrollment, passkey user verification counting as `teluni-aal2`, recovery codes, introspection reflecting session end and disablement, back-channel logout on recovery, reset-token lifetime, brute-force behavior) is a qualification item. If the pinned version cannot meet one, PJ-24 records the gap and proposes a reviewed change rather than relaxing a check.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Session Integration Design
heading: Local development assurance exception
text:
Local development assurance exception
On 2026-10-24 the owner requested optional two-step verification for local development. `TELUNI_DEV_MFA_MODE` defaults to `required`; `optional` is accepted only with `ORION_ENV=development`, a loopback API listener, and loopback public origin and issuer. The identity module repeats the environment/origin/issuer guard for direct composition. This is a testing exception to the production P12/P14 requirements, not a new authentication method or a product company policy. [Setup](../setup.md#optional-two-step-verification-during-local-development) owns activation and restart instructions.
In optional mode, login does not request AAL2 or recent authentication from Keycloak. After all ordinary session, signature, principal, CSRF, expiry and provider-revalidation checks succeed, the identity boundary projects effective strong/recent assurance for local business workflows only. It reports `assuranceLevel=teluni-development`, and the session page labels the waiver instead of claiming two-step verification. The stored provider ACR and strong-authentication timestamp are unchanged. Disabling the setting therefore restores the actual stored assurance on the next request, including for existing cookies. Other authorization and transaction checks remain active; no account credentials, authenticator enrollment or provider flow are rewritten.
The [local-mode integration test](../../apps/api/test/identity/development-mfa.test.ts) uses real Keycloak and migrated PostgreSQL to verify password-only step-up, the absence of OTP enrollment/fabricated stored assurance, enforcement after recomposition with `required`, CSRF and missing-session rejection, and logout. Configuration tests reject nondevelopment/nonloopback and invalid values; the [session-page test](../../apps/web/test/identity.browser.test.tsx) checks the explicit development label. Real environment provisioning and required-mode assurance qualification remain unchanged.

title: Teluni Implementation Plan
heading: Maintaining this plan
text:
Maintaining this plan
Every contributor or coding agent performing implementation work must maintain this plan and the [project human actions](human-actions.md) within the user's authorized scope.
Before implementation, inspect actual repository state, the relevant task, its prerequisites, governing policy, and linked human actions. Do not treat a planned capability or unchecked action as available.
Mark a task `in progress` when work actually starts. Update statuses when evidence, scope, dependencies, or blockers change, and before each handoff or completion report.
Allocate stable task IDs as `PJ-NN`; never reuse or renumber them. Add finer tasks when needed; do not hide unfinished subtasks inside a completed row.
Record concise evidence in the task row: implementation paths, validation commands and results, review references, or a linked decision. Record evidence produced for this repository—local validation, this repository's CI runs, and this repository's external settings. Do not store secret values or sensitive output.
A task becomes `completed` only when its deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence. A partial implementation or an unavailable required check is not completion.
When human intervention is necessary, add or update a project human action, link it from the affected task, mark that task `blocked`, and tell the user what is needed. Continue independent authorized work where possible.
A future prerequisite is `pending`, not automatically `blocked`.
When scope or sequencing changes, use `changed`, explain why and what replaces the work, and link supporting decisions. Do not delete unresolved obligations to make the plan look complete.
Update command availability, current documentation, generated artifacts, and the human actions in the same coherent change where applicable. Do not change ADR status merely to record implementation progress.
Status
Meaning
`pending`
Not started; includes conditional work whose trigger has not occurred.
`in progress`
Work has started and is incomplete.
`completed`
Applicable deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence.
`blocked`
The identified work cannot proceed without a recorded dependency, decision, access, or correction.
`changed`
Scope, applicability, or sequencing was explicitly revised; reason and replacement or disposition are recorded.

Retain the accepted stack recorded in the [technology map](../architecture/technology-decisions.md); incompatibilities require explicit resolution rather than silent substitution.

Keep generated artifacts reproducible and subordinate to canonical sources. Reviewed SQL migrations follow their separate release-history rules.
Require non-mutating `pnpm validate` for substantial changes, using the same capabilities locally and in CI.
